criteria.id: WorkItems can be classified by security impact, data sensitivity, permission impact, exposed API surface, dependency risk, and deployment risk
configured high-risk WorkItems require a threat model before delivery
security evidence can be ingested from tests, code review, dependency scans, secret scans, static analysis, dynamic tests, and manual reviews
missing required security controls or evidence block delivery when configured
residual risk acceptance records approver, reason, scope, expiration, and compensating controls
a project can store SLOs with availability, latency, error budget, capacity, backup, restore, and dependency assumptions
configured production-facing WorkItems require an observability plan before delivery
reliability readiness rolls up to Project and Milestone views
agent-run provenance records source inputs, model identity, skill versions, tool calls, output, and verification
AI-generated analysis records confidence, assumptions, limitations, and open questions
missing provenance blocks automated delivery claims when configured
evidence reports cover Project, Milestone, WorkItem, release, and certification scopes
reports stay draft until a human owner approves them and snapshots include timestamp, actor, source version, and export hash
reports export as JSON and Markdown
customers cannot record threat models, risk acceptances, or approve attestations
